chunks: Muhammad b. Yahya, from Muhammad b. al-Husayn, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamily, from Durust b. Abi Mansur, from Burayid b. Mu'awiya, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is not incumbent upon Allah's creatures that they recognise (Him on their own), but it is incumbent upon Allah that He introduce Himself to them, and it is incumbent upon the creatures — once He has introduced Himself to them — that they accept.

key_terms.يَعْرِفُوا: to recognise/acknowledge (God); the root ma'rifa implies personal, intimate knowledge rather than mere intellectual assent
key_terms.يَقْبَلُوا: to accept/receive; the obligation that follows divine self-disclosure
key_terms.يُعَرِّفَهُمْ: to introduce/make known; the causative form indicates God actively imparting knowledge of Himself

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the obligation of knowing God and the proof of Allah upon His creatures?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates a foundational theological principle: unaided recognition of God is not expected of creation, but Allah bears the obligation of making Himself known through revelation and guidance. Once that divine self-disclosure has been made — through the Prophet and the Imams — acceptance becomes incumbent upon those who have received it. This teaching was addressed to companions in the context of debates about religious obligation and the limits of unaided reason, affirming that divine guidance precedes human duty.
